Recurvirostra.title: A new species of the late Miocene charadriiform bird (Aves: Charadriiformes), with a summary of all Paleogene and Miocene Charadrii remains.
Recurvirostra.authors: Bochenski ZM, Wertz K, Tomek T, Gorobets L.
Recurvirostra.abstract: A new species, Cherevychnavis umanskae sp. nov., (Aves: Charadriiformes) from the late Miocene of Ukraine is described, and all known fossils of the suborder Charadrii from the Paleogene and Miocene are summarized. The combination of preserved characters allows us to assign the new species to the suborder Charadrii but its more exact systematic position remains uncertain. Morphologically, the new species is most similar to the extant Haematopus and Recurvirostra, and in terms of size to Haematopus, but it clearly differs from all extant genera of Charadrii. The current remains fill the temporal and spatial gaps in the fossil record of charadriiform birds; they constitute the first record of the Charadrii in eastern-most Europe, and add to our still insufficient knowledge of the late Miocene birds.

Rissa.title: Low Nest Success of Black-Legged Kittiwakes (<i>Rissa tridactyla</i>) at a Mainland Colony Is Not Associated With Disturbance From Walkers or Boats: Implications for Compensation for Offshore Renewables Impacts.
Rissa.authors: White PJC, Humphreys H, Grozier JM, Lane JR, Willey AM, Bokenkamp A, Schoefer NH, Wilson SJ, Rutherford RJ, Cole L, Hatsell C, Bonnici R, Owen E, Frost M, Lewis S, Diele K.
Rissa.abstract: Seabirds face a range of pressures including rising sea temperatures, declining food availability, offshore renewables and disturbances at their onshore nesting colonies. Developers of marine renewables often seek to implement compensatory measures to offset risk and enhance productivity through targeted management interventions, including reduction in disturbance. To evaluate whether such interventions could be effective at a mainland protected area in Scotland (St Abb's Head), we analysed a dataset of > 1400 kittiwake nests monitored across nine plots over 7 years (2015-19 and 2022-23) to (a) assess potential impacts of increasing numbers of walkers on cliff tops and boats operating close inshore on nest success and number of chicks fledged, and (b) assess whether productivity is sufficient to sustain the local population. We found no strong evidence that people or boat activity negatively affected nest success or number of chicks fledged. Rather, we observed weak positive correlations between human presence and both nest success and the probability of successful nests fledging more than a single chick, which potentially demonstrates a 'human shield' effect reducing predation rates. This suggests that mitigation of disturbance at this colony would not represent a viable compensation measure for kittiwakes. However, productivity (chicks per pair) across the study period was at the lower end of levels previously predicted to sustain kittiwake populations. This raises concerns

Rynchops.title: Endocranial anatomy of the charadriiformes: sensory system variation and the evolution of wing-propelled diving.
Rynchops.abstract: Just as skeletal characteristics provide clues regarding behavior of extinct vertebrates, phylogenetically-informed evaluation of endocranial morphology facilitates comparisons among extinct taxa and extant taxa with known behavioral characteristics. Previous research has established that endocranial morphology varies across Aves; however, variation of those systems among closely related species remains largely unexplored. The Charadriiformes (shorebirds and allies) are an ecologically diverse clade with a comparatively rich fossil record, and therefore, are well suited for investigating interspecies variation, and potential links between endocranial morphology, phylogeny, ecology and other life history attributes. Endocranial endocasts were rendered from high resolution X-ray computed tomography data for 17 charadriiforms (15 extant and two flightless extinct species). Evaluation of endocranial character state changes on a phylogeny for Charadriiformes resulted in identification of characters that vary in taxa with distinct feeding and locomotor ecologies. In comparison with all other charadriiforms, stem and crown clade wing-propelled diving Pan-Alcidae displayed compressed semicircular canals, and indistinct occipital sinuses and cerebellar fissures. Flightless wing-propelled divers have relatively smaller brains for their body mass and smaller optic lobes than volant pan-alcids. Observed differences between volant and flightless wing-propelled sister taxa are striking giv

Rynchops.title: Did pterosaurs feed by skimming? Physical modelling and anatomical evaluation of an unusual feeding method.
Rynchops.authors: Humphries S, Bonser RH, Witton MP, Martill DM.
Rynchops.abstract: Similarities between the anatomies of living organisms are often used to draw conclusions regarding the ecology and behaviour of extinct animals. Several pterosaur taxa are postulated to have been skim-feeders based largely on supposed convergences of their jaw anatomy with that of the modern skimming bird, Rynchops spp. Using physical and mathematical models of Rynchops bills and pterosaur jaws, we show that skimming is considerably more energetically costly than previously thought for Rynchops and that pterosaurs weighing more than one kilogram would not have been able to skim at all. Furthermore, anatomical comparisons between the highly specialised skull of Rynchops and those of postulated skimming pterosaurs suggest that even smaller forms were poorly adapted for skim-feeding. Our results refute the hypothesis that some pterosaurs commonly used skimming as a foraging method and illustrate the pitfalls involved in extrapolating from limited morphological convergence.

Rynchops.title: The function of the cranial crest and jaws of a unique pterosaur from the Early Cretaceous of Brazil.
Rynchops.abstract: The discovery of a previously undescribed pterosaur, Thalassodromeus sethi, yields information on the function of cranial crests and the feeding strategy developed by these extinct flying reptiles. The material consists of a large skull (length: 1420 millimeters, including the crest) with a huge bony crest that was well irrigated by blood vessels and may have been used for regulation of its body temperature. The rostrum consists of two bladelike laminae, the arrangement of which is analogous to the condition found in the bird Rynchops, which skims over the water to catch food, indicating that T. sethi also may have been a skimmer.

Scopus.title: Air pollution and adverse birth outcomes: a narrative review of epidemiological and mechanistic findings.
Scopus.authors: Hahad O, Kuntic M, Al-Kindi S, Lelieveld J, Cheng Y, Schmitt VH, Hobohm L, Keller K, Kerahrodi JG, Faridi S, Morakkabati-Spitz N, Fieß A, Daiber A, Münzel T, Bous M, Goedicke-Fritz S, Zemlin M, Nourkami-Tutdibi N, Tutdibi E.
Scopus.journal: Journal of environmental health science & engineering
Scopus.abstract: Air pollution remains a significant global health challenge and is increasingly recognized as a critical exposomic risk factor for adverse birth outcomes. Although numerous epidemiological studies have linked prenatal air pollution exposure to low birth weight, preterm birth, and stillbirth, important uncertainties remain regarding the underlying biological mechanisms, critical exposure windows, and the interplay between different pollutants and susceptibility factors. This narrative review synthesizes epidemiological findings and mechanistic evidence identified through literature searches in PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science to provide a comprehensive overview of how maternal exposure to air pollutants affects fetal development and pregnancy outcomes. The reviewed epidemiological evidence largely supports an association between maternal air pollution exposure and adverse birth outcomes. For example, a 10 µg/m3 increase in fine particulate matter (PM2.5) exposure during the second trimester has been associated with an 11.8 g reduction in birth weight and a 23.1% increase in the risk of preterm birth. Oxidative stress, inflammation, endocrine disruption, vascular dysfunction, and epigenetic modifications are considered key biological pathways through which air pollution may impair placental function, alter fetal growth trajectories, and increase the likelihood of pregnancy complications. The placenta serves as a critical interface between maternal and fetal health and is part

Scopus.title: A scoping review of turmeric adulteration based on data from six continents.
Scopus.authors: Gafner S, Orhan N, Kahraman Ç, Blumenthal M.
Scopus.abstract: ContextTurmeric (Curcuma longa) is widely used as a spice and in dietary/food supplements and herbal medicines. Reports assessing the authenticity of commercial products have shown that the ingredient is subject to adulteration with, among others, artificial dyes, undeclared diluents, and synthetic curcumin.ObjectiveThis scoping review summarizes published data on adulteration of turmeric products sold as spice and dietary or food supplements to estimate the prevalence of non-authentic turmeric on the market.MethodsThis scoping review was based on a literature analysis from Google Scholar, PubMed, ScienceDirect, Scopus, and Web of Science databases, covering publications from 2000 to 2025. Article selection was performed according to PRISMA-ScR guidelines. After the initial search, specific countries were added to refine the search. Of the 375 publications retrieved, 347 were eliminated as duplicates or because they lacked information on turmeric adulteration, adulteration of commercial products, or did not provide the number of adulterated samples. An additional 19 papers were found searching the citations, or by using Google Search with the keywords "Curcuma longa", "turmeric", "government report", and "adulteration". One more report from the CVUA Stuttgart was found using the keywords "Kurkuma", "Verfälschung", and "Report". In total, 48 papers were included in the review.ResultsA total of 48 publications representing 2235 commercial turmeric samples were included in the s

Scopus.title: Data-Driven Design of Fire-Safe Vinyl Ester Composites with Mineral and Inorganic Additives: A Systematic Review.
Scopus.authors: Iztleuova B, Kandola BK, Bekeshev A, Zhanturina N, Akhmetova M, Wang X.
Scopus.abstract: Vinyl ester resins are used in marine, wind energy, and chemical plant composites, yet their styrene-rich network burns readily. This review examines how mineral and inorganic additives (clays, layered hydroxides, metal hydroxides, phosphates, silica and silsesquioxanes, and natural minerals) alter the thermal degradation and fire behaviour of vinyl ester composites. Following PRISMA 2020, 962 Scopus records were screened, 697 full texts assessed, and 1255 formulations from 235 studies extracted into a curated, quality-flagged dataset. The decomposition pathway of the vinyl ester network is synthesised, and condensed- and gas-phase mechanisms are linked to the evidence that distinguishes them. Minerals act mainly in the condensed phase; the largest within-study gains come from phosphorus chemistry, in inorganic phosphates or mineral-organic hybrids, usually at loadings at which strength decreases. Machine-learning models of within-study changes, validated on held-out studies, explain half of the variance in the reduction in total heat release (R2 ≈ 0.50) and a third in the change in limiting oxygen index (R2 ≈ 0.37), enough to rank formulations but not to replace fire tests, and they do not predict the UL-94 rating, indicating that differences between studies, rather than the choice of model, limit data-driven design. Under-studied minerals, minimum reporting requirements, and research priorities are identified.

Scopus.title: <i>Equisetum arvense</i> in Disorders Associated with Oxidative Stress and Inflammation: Ethnomedicinal Uses, Phytochemistry, Pharmacological Mechanisms, and Translational Potential.
Scopus.abstract: Equisetum arvense is traditionally used for urinary complaints, inflammation, and tissue repair. However, the links between its traditional uses, phytochemistry, disease-related mechanisms, and clinical evidence remain insufficiently integrated. This review addresses this gap through an oxidative stress- and inflammation-centered synthesis. Flavonoids, phenolic acids, and other horsetail constituents may exert antioxidant and anti-inflammatory effects by scavenging radicals, enhancing antioxidant defenses, and modulating NF-κB and MAPK signaling. Findings suggest potential applications across urinary, inflammatory, metabolic, and musculoskeletal disorders. Integrating traditional indications with experimental and clinical findings highlights differences in evidence maturity and identifies extract variability, uncertain constituent contributions, and limited clinical mechanistic validation as major translational barriers. E. arvense shows therapeutic potential, but supporting evidence is predominantly preclinical. Standardized preparations, targeted mechanistic studies, and rigorous clinical trials incorporating oxidative stress and inflammatory biomarkers are needed to establish efficacy, optimal dosing, and long-term safety. Literature was retrieved from PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, ScienceDirect, and Google Scholar. Relevant studies were screened and narratively evaluated according to evidence type, extract characterization, model relevance, and mechanistic support.

Scopus.title: The Sustainability of the Beef Supply Chain: An AI-Aided Systematic Literature Review.
Scopus.authors: Belperio S, Petti R, Dolfi E, Masi M, Cavallini D, Palmonari A, Mammi LME, Niero G, Vecchio Y, Costa A, De Marchi M, Formigoni A, Adinolfi F, Visentin G.
Scopus.abstract: The sustainability of the beef supply chain is increasingly being investigated due to its environmental impacts, economic challenges, and growing societal concerns regarding animal welfare. Although the scientific literature has extensively addressed these issues, the environmental, economic, and social dimensions of sustainability have often been investigated from different perspectives and across separate research areas, limiting an integrated understanding of sustainability across the beef supply chain. To address this gap, this systematic literature review organizes the available evidence to answer the following research question: What are the sustainability aspects of the beef supply chain? Following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) framework, 2608 records were retrieved from the Scopus database in April 2025, and 1534 of them were screened with the support of the open-access, artificial intelligence-aided software ASReview LAB. Overall, 539 relevant publications (1988-2025) were included in the bibliometric and keyword-network analyses, while 105 studies underwent content analysis and were classified according to four dimensions of sustainable meat production: (i) improving production efficiency, (ii) mitigating greenhouse gas emissions, (iii) agroecology and farming ecosystems, and (iv) socio-cultural, animal welfare, and ethical aspects. Research output increased markedly after 2018, while environmental themes, particular

Scopus.title: <i>Acrocomia aculeata</i> Beyond Biodiesel: Biotechnological Applications in Food, Health, Fermentation and Animal Nutrition-A Scoping Review.
Scopus.authors: Marques de Paula UL, Costa DDS, Santos FDCV, Silva AJRD, Moreno DSA.
Scopus.abstract: Although Acrocomia aculeata (macaúba) is primarily recognized as a promising biodiesel feedstock, its biological resources offer opportunities in food, health, fermentation, and sustainable technologies. This scoping review, complemented by a narrative synthesis, mapped original research published from January 2010 to 30 July 2026. PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched, and eligible studies were classified by their primary research focus. Of 1320 records identified, 365 publications were included in the thematic mapping, including 54 classified under human and animal health. Research on cultivation and production for biofuel applications predominated (61.6%), followed by human and animal health (14.8%), plant ecology and biology (11.2%), bioremediation and sustainability (6.3%), and other applications (6.0%). Within the health category, investigated biological activity represented 50.0%, livestock production and feed 20.4%, human nutrition and prebiotic applications 18.5%, and fermentation processes, beverage preservation, and probiotic applications 11.1%. Preclinical investigations have examined anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, antimicrobial, antitumor, hypoglycemic, photoprotective, and antithrombotic activities. However, further mechanistic, toxicological, clinical, and process-standardization studies are needed to establish safety, efficacy, and scalable applications.

Scopus.title: Invisible exposure, visible harm: air pollution and the global burden of cardiovascular disease.
Scopus.authors: Thakur N, Biswas H, Das A, Thakur S, Ghosh R.
Scopus.journal: Genes and environment : the official journal of the Japanese Environmental Mutagen Society
Scopus.abstract: BackgroundAir pollution is a major modifiable environmental risk factor for cardiovascular disease (CVD). In the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2021 study, air pollution was the second-leading risk factor for death worldwide, accounting for an estimated 8.1 million deaths from all causes in 2021, and particulate matter (PM) pollution (ambient plus household) was associated with approximately 4.5 million cardiovascular deaths.Main bodyThis narrative review, based on a structured search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus and Web of Science, summarizes evidence on the sources of the main pollutants (fine particulate matter [PM₂.₅], coarse particulate matter [PM₁₀], ultrafine particles [PM₀.₁/UFP], nitrogen dioxide [NO₂], sulfur dioxide [SO₂], ozone [O₃] and carbon monoxide [CO]); the global burden of pollution-attributable CVD; epidemiological evidence from major cohort and multi-city studies; biological mechanisms, distinguishing those supported by human data from those derived mainly from cell and animal models; the associations with specific cardiovascular phenotypes (ischemic heart disease, stroke, hypertension, heart failure, arrhythmia and vascular disease); susceptible populations; transcriptomic, proteomic, lipidomic, epigenetic and microRNA findings; and preventive strategies graded by strength of evidence. Observational studies consistently associate short- and long-term exposure to PM₂.₅ with cardiovascular events and mortality, and controlled-exposure, quasi-experimental and

Scopus.title: Rethinking the sustainability assessment of grass-fed beef: a holistic systematic review.
Scopus.authors: Mazungunye PP, Saruchera M, Mudavanhu S, Dzama K, Mapiye C.
Scopus.abstract: Consumer demand for grass-fed beef (GFB) is increasing due to its perceived advantages in food safety, healthfulness, animal welfare, and environmental stewardship, yet its sustainability remains contested. This PRISMA-guided systematic review synthesised evidence from 141 studies identified through Web of Science, Scopus, AGRICOLA, and supplementary grey-literature sources to evaluate GFB production, meat quality, and sustainability, and to provide actionable insights for future research, market governance, and policy. The currently inconsistent evidence is insufficient to confirm the sustainability of GFB. Although GFB can offer desirable quality attributes, including leaner carcasses, greater proportions of omega-3 and conjugated linoleic fatty acids, and elevated antioxidant levels, its darker colour and variable tenderness may affect consumer acceptance. Environmentally, reduced grain inputs and greater pasture biodiversity may promote ecological stewardship, but methane emissions and higher land requirements may offset these gains unless adaptive grazing and carbon sequestration are appropriately incorporated. Socially, animal welfare can be enhanced through regenerative grazing practices but can also be compromised when animals are exposed to adverse weather and parasites. Economic performance depends on productivity, certification costs, price premiums, and market access. Despite their growing social relevance, animal welfare, traceability, authenticity, and certifica

Scopus.title: Global Poultry Feed Protein Sources: Trends, Challenges, and Sustainability Perspectives Using FAOSTAT Data.
Scopus.journal: Journal of animal physiology and animal nutrition
Scopus.abstract: The global poultry industry is one of the fastest-growing livestock sectors, with worldwide chicken stocks exceeding 32 billion heads and meat production surpassing 144 million tonnes in 2024 (FAOSTAT, 2026). Conventional protein sources, particularly soybean meal (SBM) and fishmeal, underpin most commercial poultry diets but face mounting challenges related to environmental sustainability, supply-chain volatility, and land-use pressures. This systematic review evaluates global trends in poultry feed protein sources using FAOSTAT production and trade data (2000-2024), alongside evidence from 57 peer-reviewed publications identified through a PRISMA-compliant, multi-database search. A structured literature search was conducted across Web of Science (WoS), Scopus, and PubMed using consistent search logic combining poultry, protein-source, and sustainability/nutrition/feed terms. Searches yielded 122 (WoS), 5920 (Scopus), and 1827 (PubMed) records (7869 total; 6215 unique after removing ineligible document types and DOI-matched duplicates). The qualitative synthesis presented here is based on the original WoS-driven screening pipeline (57 included studies); the wider Scopus/PubMed pool was used as a supplementary coverage check rather than fully re-screened, a limitation discussed in Section 4.6. FAOSTAT data sets on chicken stocks, meat production, soybean production, and soybean trade were analysed for 2000-2024. Global chicken stocks grew from ~14.8 billion head in 2000 to ~3

Scopus.title: Polymeric Materials for Ophthalmic Lenses: A Systematic Review on Structure, Properties, Manufacturing and Sustainability.
Scopus.authors: Calvi M, Baldini E, Minotto MM, Moro D, Gagliardi V, Santandrea D, Beghetto V.
Scopus.abstract: Polymeric materials have largely replaced mineral glass in ophthalmic lenses owing to their low density, impact resistance, optical performance, and manufacturing versatility. Despite their widespread use, the available literature remains fragmented, with individual studies primarily addressing specific polymer families, optical performance, manufacturing technologies, or surface coatings rather than providing an integrated overview of ophthalmic lens materials. This systematic review critically examines the relationships between chemical structure and molecular architecture of ophthalmic lens polymers and their optical, mechanical, thermal, and processing properties. The literature published between 2000 and 2026 was searched in Web of Science, Scopus, ScienceDirect, and PubMed, following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, and 91 documents were included. Properties of poly(diethylene glycol bis(allyl carbonate)) (CR-39®), polycarbonate, poly(methyl methacrylate), poly(urethane-urea) (Trivex®), and high-refractive-index poly(thiourethane) systems are reported, with particular attention to refractive index, chromatic dispersion, impact resistance, durability, processability, and coating compatibility. Surface-engineering approaches, digital manufacturing, market developments, and environmental challenges associated with production waste and end-of-life management are also evaluated. The analysis identifies persistent trade-offs between optical performance, mechanical durability, manufact

Scopus.title: Plant-Derived Functional Molecules for Photoelectrochemical Water Splitting: From Molecular Design to Hybrid Materials Engineering.
Scopus.authors: Kim S, Hwang I, Kim G, Yoon H.
Scopus.abstract: Plant-derived molecules offer tunable coordination and surface chemistry for photoelectrochemical (PEC) water splitting. A Scopus survey retrieved 45 documents linking both topics in 2005-2025, equivalent to 0.34% of the PEC literature. A supplementary search added 15 records, and screening retained 26 research articles. The review organizes molecular functions into light harvesting, charge-transfer mediation, coordination of catalytic overlayers, and passivation. A molecular readiness scale and a validation protocol connect molecular identity to verified device performance. Hybrid layers combining plant ligands with Co, Ni, or Fe raised BiVO4 photocurrents to approximately 3-6 mA cm-2 at 1.23 V vs. the reversible hydrogen electrode (RHE). Comparable inorganic overlayers preclude a general claim of superior activity. Ambient solution processing and control of interfacial coordination provide the principal design opportunities. Two-electron phenol/quinone potentials do not establish the feasibility of one-electron hole relay, which requires independent kinetic and redox evidence. At a coverage of 0.1 nmol cm-2, a chlorophyll layer has a calculated photocurrent upper bound of approximately 0.05 mA cm-2 within 640-680 nm alone. Broadband enhancement requires wavelength-resolved attribution. Operation for 1000 h at 1 mA cm-2 and a loading of 1 nmol cm-2 corresponds to approximately 3.7 × 107 electrons per initially loaded molecule. The proposed framework links molecular structure

Scopus.title: Integrated Biorefineries for Food Waste and Food-Processing Side Streams Through Feedstock-Oriented Design and Sustainable Process Integration.
Scopus.authors: Lazăr Coșbuc ED, Oprea Blanaru PS, Ungureanu-Comăniță ED, Teodosiu C, Gavrilescu M.
Scopus.abstract: Food waste represents a renewable carbon resource with considerable potential for the production of bioenergy, platform chemicals, biomaterials, and other high-value products within integrated biorefinery systems. However, the heterogeneous composition of food waste, together with the diversity of available conversion technologies, complicates the selection of efficient and economically viable valorization strategies. Successful food-waste valorization requires a systems-oriented approach that integrates individual technologies with feedstock characteristics, pretreatment, conversion pathways, and resource recovery into coherent biorefinery configurations. This structured critical review synthesizes literature identified through Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection, and ScienceDirect for the period January 2015-September 2026, and critically examines the evolution of food-waste biorefinery concepts from conventional processing to integrated, cascade, circular, and near-zero-waste systems, highlighting their engineering principles, advantages, and limitations. Current pretreatment technologies and biological, chemical and thermochemical conversion pathways are comparatively evaluated with respect to process performance, technology readiness and industrial applicability. Particular attention is given to integrated biorefinery design, emphasizing feedstock-oriented process selection, cascade valorization, process integration and resource recovery. The complementary roles of li

Spheniscus.title: The skull of the Miocene Spheniscus urbinai (Aves, Sphenisciformes): osteology, brain morphology, and the cranial pneumatic systems.
Spheniscus.authors: Acosta Hospitaleche C, Paulina-Carabajal A, Yury-Yáñez R.
Spheniscus.abstract: Spheniscus urbinai represents one of four extinct Spheniscus species from the Cenozoic of southern South America, known from several poorly described diversely complete skulls and postcranial elements. Here, we present a review of the cranial osteology of all known specimens (collected in Argentina, Chile, and Peru), including a paleoneurological analysis using CT scans, and an exploration of its cranial pneumaticity compared to other extinct and living seabirds. Our results show that among Spheniscus species, S. urbinai exhibits slightly greater cranial pneumaticity than the living species. Additionally, we confirm previous findings which indicate that the marked reduction of cranial pneumaticity-which is characteristic of living penguins-occurred early during the Eocene (as observed in the Antarctic penguin MLP 12-I-20-1, but not in the coeval Anthropornis).

Spheniscus.title: Evidence for the Loss of Pneumatization and Pneumosteal Tissues in Secondarily Aquatic Archosaurs.
Spheniscus.authors: Byrne PJ, Smith ND, Schachner ER, Bottjer DJ, Huttenlocker AK.
Spheniscus.abstract: The evolutionary origins of the avian air sac pulmonary system are enigmatic due to the rarity of soft-tissue preservation in fossils. Here, we test whether fine anchoring fibers on the endosteal bone of bird and non-avian dinosaur vertebrae-termed "pneumosteum"-are absent in taxa lacking pneumatic openings. We studied thin sections from the caudalmost cervical and cranial dorsal vertebrae of 21 extant amniotes to infer the presence or absence of invading diverticula through vertebral foramina. We also provide a differential diagnosis of the structural features of pneumosteum. We found that the secondarily aquatic Western grebe (Aechmophorus occidentalis) and Magellanic penguin (Spheniscus magellanicus) lack external pneumaticity and pneumosteum. In addition, the small passerine bird examined (Estrildidae spp.) exhibits invading diverticula but no pneumosteum. This suggests that ventilatory air sacs and associated diverticula can be present despite the absence of osteological and histologic correlates and that these features are lost when transitioning to an aquatic lifestyle or in small-bodied birds. In volant pneumatized birds, diverticula and pneumosteum are associated with pneumatic foramina. This suggests that, in fossil birds, pneumatic foramina are good indicators of the presence of pulmonary diverticula. Furthermore, the loss of invading respiratory diverticula and pneumatic osteological characters in the postcranial skeleton of pursuit diving birds serves as a remind

Spheniscus.title: Penguin osteohistology, the key role of the Internal Circumferential Layer in gender determination
Spheniscus.authors: Garat LM, Talevi M, Hospitaleche CA.
Spheniscus.abstract: Abstract  This study investigates the osteohistological variation in Sphenisciformes, focusing on the microstructural patterns associated with medullary bone (MB) and the inner circumferential layer (ICL) across several species, including Aptenodytes forsteri, Pygoscelis antarctica, P. papua and Spheniscus magellanicus. Histological sections of both appendicular and axial skeletons were analysed, revealing significant variations in the presence of MB and ICL across taxa. We aimed to expand the understanding of microanatomy and histology in Sphenisciformes by describing these variations and testing a hypothesis regarding sexual dimorphism based on ICL presence. Key findings include the identification of MB in all specimens, while S. magellanicus exhibited a more limited distribution of MB. Additionally, females of P. antarctica and A. forsteri had an ICL, although this layer was partially remodelled due to osteoclastic activity linked to egg-laying. These findings contribute to the ongoing discussion of gender discrimination in extant and extinct penguin taxa and highlight the importance of MB and ICL in understanding reproductive and developmental histories. Our results suggest that, although the ICL may not be an absolute indicator of sex, its absence or remodelling in adult individuals may serve as a useful tool to differentiate females, even in the fossil record. Furthermore, the variability in MB distribution in S. magellanicus suggests dietary influences, specifically ca

Spheniscus.title: An integrative insight into the synsacral canal of fossil and extant Antarctic penguins.
Spheniscus.authors: Jadwiszczak P, Svensson-Marcial A, Mörs T.
Spheniscus.abstract: The lumbosacral-canal system in birds most likely operates as a sense organ involved in the control of balanced walking and perching, but our knowledge of it is superficial. Penguins constitute interesting objects for the study of this system due to their upright walking, but only the Humboldt penguin, Spheniscus humboldti, and some incomplete fossil penguin synsacra have been studied in this respect. Here, we give an integrative comparative insight into the synsacral canal of extant Emperor penguin, Aptenodytes forsteri, Adelie penguin, Pygoscelis adeliae, and Eocene giant Anthropornis and/or Palaeeudyptes Antarctic penguins, using computed tomography imaging and associated data-extraction methodologies, complemented by analytical approaches ranging from geometric morphometrics to modularity, curvature, and wavelet analyses. We document that the variability in the number of synsacro-lumbar vertebrae is evolutionarily conserved, and all studied synsacra possess osteological correlates of the lumbosacral-canal system. We also found that Eocene and extant Antarctic penguins were separable on the basis of the main direction of the shape-related (size-independent) variability within said system, and A. forsteri was unique in the entire studied set in terms of the relative cranial shift of this compound structure. Moreover, we suggest that the evolutionary processes, shaping both the terrestrial posture and gait, were responsible, in extant penguins, for the increased simplicity a

Spheniscus.title: Bone histology in extant and fossil penguins (Aves: Sphenisciformes).
Spheniscus.authors: Ksepka DT, Werning S, Sclafani M, Boles ZM.
Spheniscus.abstract: Substantial changes in bone histology accompany the secondary adaptation to life in the water. This transition is well documented in several lineages of mammals and non-avian reptiles, but has received relatively little attention in birds. This study presents new observations on the long bone microstructure of penguins, based on histological sections from two extant taxa (Spheniscus and Aptenodytes) and eight fossil specimens belonging to stem lineages (†Palaeospheniscus and several indeterminate Eocene taxa). High bone density in penguins results from compaction of the internal cortical tissues, and thus penguin bones are best considered osteosclerotic rather than pachyostotic. Although the oldest specimens sampled in this study represent stages of penguin evolution that occurred at least 25 million years after the loss of flight, major differences in humeral structure were observed between these Eocene stem taxa and extant taxa. This indicates that the modification of flipper bone microstructure continued long after the initial loss of flight in penguins. It is proposed that two key transitions occurred during the shift from the typical hollow avian humerus to the dense osteosclerotic humerus in penguins. First, a reduction of the medullary cavity occurred due to a decrease in the amount of perimedullary osteoclastic activity. Second, a more solid cortex was achieved by compaction. In extant penguins and †Palaeospheniscus, most of the inner cortex is formed by rapid osteoge

Spheniscus.title: Longer and less overlapping food webs in anthropogenically disturbed marine ecosystems: confirmations from the past.
Spheniscus.authors: Saporiti F, Bearhop S, Silva L, Vales DG, Zenteno L, Crespo EA, Aguilar A, Cardona L.
Spheniscus.abstract: The human exploitation of marine resources is characterised by the preferential removal of the largest species. Although this is expected to modify the structure of food webs, we have a relatively poor understanding of the potential consequences of such alteration. Here, we take advantage of a collection of ancient consumer tissues, using stable isotope analysis and SIBER to assess changes in the structure of coastal marine food webs in the South-western Atlantic through the second half of the Holocene as a result of the sequential exploitation of marine resources by hunter-gatherers, western sealers and modern fishermen. Samples were collected from shell middens and museums. Shells of both modern and archaeological intertidal herbivorous molluscs were used to reconstruct changes in the stable isotopic baseline, while modern and archaeological bones of the South American sea lion Otaria flavescens, South American fur seal Arctocephalus australis and Magellanic penguin Spheniscus magellanicus were used to analyse changes in the structure of the community of top predators. We found that ancient food webs were shorter, more redundant and more overlapping than current ones, both in northern-central Patagonia and southern Patagonia. These surprising results may be best explained by the huge impact of western sealing on pinnipeds during the fur trade period, rather than the impact of fishing on fish populations. As a consequence, the populations of pinnipeds at the end of the seali

Spheniscus.title: Multiple cenozoic invasions of Africa by penguins (Aves, Sphenisciformes).
Spheniscus.abstract: Africa hosts a single breeding species of penguin today, yet the fossil record indicates that a diverse array of now-extinct taxa once inhabited southern African coastlines. Here, we show that the African penguin fauna had a complex history involving multiple dispersals and extinctions. Phylogenetic analyses and biogeographic reconstructions incorporating new fossil material indicate that, contrary to previous hypotheses, the four Early Pliocene African penguin species do not represent an endemic radiation or direct ancestors of the living Spheniscus demersus (blackfooted penguin). A minimum of three dispersals to Africa, probably assisted by the eastward-flowing Antarctic Circumpolar and South Atlantic currents, occurred during the Late Cenozoic. As regional sea-level fall eliminated islands and reduced offshore breeding areas during the Pliocene, all but one penguin lineage ended in extinction, resulting in today's depleted fauna.

Spheniscus.title: Morphometric patterns in Recent and fossil penguins (Aves, Sphenisciformes).
Spheniscus.abstract: A total of 622 skin specimens, 527 skeletons, and myological data compiled by Schreiweis (1972) were used to investigate morphometric patterns within and among the 18 Recent species of Spheniscidae, and to compare the family with a fighted species, the common diving-petrel (Pelecanoides urinator), considered by some authorities to be similar to the flighted ancestor of penguins. Fossil penguins also were studied using measurements from 111 skeletal elements representing 18 species. Most external and skeletal measurements follow interspecific rankings in body mass; the latter span a 30-fold range from 1 kg in Eudyptula minor to 30 kg in Aptenodytes forsteri. Flighted Pelecanoides is only one-tenth the mass of the smallest spheniscid. Wing areas and body masses of penguins maintain approximate geometric similitude among species; the allometric coefficient is 0.62 ± 0.04. Several skeletal elements are less derived in conformation in the fossil penguins than in modern confamilials. Despite great variation in the lengths of wing and leg skeletons, penguins show relative consistency in proportions of wing elements; pelvic proportions were more variable within the Spheniscidae. Proportions within both limbs are distinctly different from those of Pelecanoides. Analysis of correlation structures within species of penguin revealed three major subsets of skeletal variables that are highly intercorrelated: trunk-skull lengths, appendicular-trunk widths, and appendicular lengths.
